headline: High: shared broad network egress and overlapping file/CLI surfaces create data-leak and conflict risks; prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented: agent_a uses API/MCP-compatible client support, while agent_b has stdin/stdout and filesystem I/O but use_mcp is false. A prompt-injection bridge would require unusual manual copy/paste or external orchestration, so the pathway exists but is not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b stdin/stdout without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator writes agent_a output into a file that agent_b reads as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter and treat agent_a output as untrusted text.
Disable manual copy/paste between agents during shared tasks.
Require a human review step before agent_b executes any instruction-like text.
Log and flag any agent_a output containing tool directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches API keys and web content and has broad network egress; agent_b reads/writes filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials plus private keys. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive data if outputs or files are exchanged through the filesystem or operator workflow. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a output containing API keys or web content is saved into a path agent_b can read, leakage is possible.
IF agent_b writes extracted secrets into a shared directory later uploaded or transmitted by agent_a, leakage is possible.
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b on separate workspaces.
Do not pass secrets through shared files or stdout.
Redact API keys and private keys before any handoff.
Restrict outbound network access for tasks that do not require it.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent_a can call APIs and supports multiple instances. They do not both have explicit same-dir write or git mutation, so high is not justified, but overlapping mutable surfaces still create race and overwrite risk if they share artifacts or a workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same output directory, file overwrites or partial writes can occur.
IF an orchestrator reuses the same mutable artifact path across runs, conflicts become likely.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent.
Serialize writes to any shared artifact.
Use temporary per-run filenames.
Avoid concurrent execution on the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces scraped web content and structured data; agent_b can consume files and execute shell commands. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, a bad scrape or injected content can cascade into incorrect container analysis or unsafe commands. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as input without validation, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a scrapes malformed or adversarial content and agent_b executes derived commands, cascading failure is likely.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all agent_a outputs.
Have a human verify high-impact fields before agent_b acts.
Reject command generation from untrusted scraped text.
Keep a checksum or provenance record for transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks against source URLs.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles API keys and web content with broad egress; agent_b handles registry credentials, private keys, and environment variables while running shell commands. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because sensitive data classes are clearly present on both sides, medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF either agent processes regulated data such as customer secrets or private keys, retention and logging controls must match.
IF agent_a sends sensitive content to a third-party API while agent_b stores it locally, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Confirm both agents' retention settings before use.
Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Disable verbose logging for secret-bearing tasks.
Store secrets only in approved secret managers.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries for both agents.
